title: Natural-Effect Estimation in Mediation under Polynomial Overlap Tails
banked_reason: The note proves the oracle n^-2/3 rate and two learned-law lower bounds on a single diagnostic parameter slice; neither learned-law risk has a sharp class-wide rate.
gap_reasons: The note proves the oracle n^-2/3 rate and two learned-law lower bounds on a single diagnostic parameter slice.
Its n^-4/13 upper bound applies only to a restricted, partly supplied subexperiment, so neither learned-law risk has a sharp class-wide rate.

The n^-8/45 fully learned lower bound establishes separation from oracle risk but does not establish an additional price for learning the source law, because the ratio of the two learned-law risks remains unresolved.
proof_attempt_summary: The source-attested D0.5 review passed mathematics and decision checks. Discovery proved the diagnostic oracle n^-2/3 rate, target-law n^-4/13 and fully learned n^-8/45 lower bounds, and their polynomial separations from oracle; a localized estimator attains n^-4/13 only on a fixed-cell subexperiment. The field claim failed because no class-wide learned-law upper bound or additional source-law learning price was established; a uniform estimator for arbitrary low-density geometry remains a substantial open problem.
tldr: For the identified natural-effect mean under exact polynomial transport tails, the diagnostic class has oracle risk \(n^{-2/3}\), target-law-learned risk at least \(n^{-4/13}\), and fully learned risk at least \(n^{-8/45}\). Both learned-law risks are polynomially larger than the oracle benchmark. Sharp learned-law orders, their mutual ratio, and the full parameter-domain frontier remain open.
gap: Fixed-policy local minimax theory covers a related scalar linear functional, but checked results do not characterize the global three-information-regime risk for the same Bernoulli natural-effect functional over separately Hölder mediator densities and two-sided polynomial ratio tails.
fill: Verify the oracle and target-learning benchmarks, resolve the conditional three-level source-learning test, and determine global sharp risks with concrete estimators or a rigorous obstruction.
